SOURCE: The High School Magazine (Montreal, 1916), the centenary number of the Royal Grammar
        School / High School of Montreal. Internet Archive item highschoolmagazi00high.
        NOT lending-restricted; full djvu text downloaded and searched 2026-09-06.
        "Kanawana" occurs exactly once, at line 7034, in the advertisement pages.

=== THE ADVERTISEMENT (djvu text lines 7028-7052) ===
CONDCCTED  BY 
K  A  M  P 
Kanawana 
for  BOYS 
Open  June  24th  to 
August  12th 
The  Cost, 
S5.00  per  week 
^Efje  iHontreal  goung  iilen's  Christian 
Association 
For  further  information,  apply  to  any  Branch 
of  the  Y.  M.  C.  A. 

READ AS SET: an advertisement occupying part of the first advertising page (the Contents
  gives 'Advertisements ... 52'), reading:

      AN IDEAL PLACE for YOUR BOY
      CONDUCTED BY
      KAMP Kanawana  for BOYS
      Open June 24th to August 12th
      The Cost, $5.00 per week
      The Montreal Young Men's Christian Association
      For further information, apply to any Branch of the Y.M.C.A.

  (The OCR gives 'CONDCCTED', 'S5.00' for $5.00, and renders the Association's name in the
   blackletter-derived garble "^Efje iHontreal goung iilen's Christian Association", which is
   the standard OCR failure on Old English type and is read here as 'The Montreal Young Men's
   Christian Association'.)

WHAT IT ESTABLISHES: the 1916 season ran 24 JUNE to 12 AUGUST -- seven weeks -- at $5.00 A
  WEEK, advertised to the boys of the High School of Montreal and their parents, with
  enquiries taken at any YMCA branch rather than at the camp.

================================================================================
A CAUTION ABOUT THE PAGE BEFORE IT.

  The article immediately preceding the advertisements is "A Week in the Woods" (Contents,
  pp. 47-51), an unsigned canoe-trip narrative. It is tempting, and it is NOT attributed to
  Kanawana here. It never names a camp, never names the Y.M.C.A., and names its route only by
  lakes: Lac Diable, Lac Cypres, Lac Daby, Lac Clef, Lac Caribou, Lac Boisfranc, Lac Bois,
  Lac Batiment and Lake McLaren. It does mention a "dining pavilion" and an "Old Guard", and
  the Kanawana advertisement is the next thing on the page -- but an advertisement's position
  is bought, not editorial, and adjacency is not attribution. If the route can be placed
  against Kanawana's known trip country the question reopens; until then it is a High School
  of Montreal canoe trip and nothing more.

  THE ROUTE HAS SINCE BEEN PLACED, 2026-09-06, against Natural Resources Canada's geographical
  names service (geogratis.gc.ca/services/geoname). Five of the nine lakes land in one tight
  block in the LAC-LEGENDRE and SAINT-DONAT country of the MATAWINIE regional county
  municipality:

      Lac du Diable    Lac-Legendre, Matawinie   46.548 N  74.290 W   78 km from Kanawana
      Lac Batiment     Lac-Legendre, Matawinie   46.522 N  74.297 W   75 km
      Lac McLaren      Lac-Legendre, Matawinie   46.511 N  74.234 W   73 km
      Lac des Cypres   Lac-Legendre, Matawinie   46.504 N  74.195 W   73 km
      Lac la Clef      Saint-Donat, Matawinie    46.384 N  74.219 W   59 km

  Cluster centre 46.494 N, 74.247 W -- about SEVENTY-TWO KILOMETRES NORTH of Kanawana
  (45.851 N, 74.194 W). LAC BATIMENT AND LAC McLAREN ARE EACH UNIQUE IN THE PROVINCE, which is
  what makes the identification firm rather than a coincidence of common lake names -- the same
  kind of control that Kanawyer, California, provided for the postal list.

  "Lac Daby" and "Lac Boisfranc" return nothing from that service or from a web search, and are
  probably OCR manglings or unofficial local names. "Lac Bois" and "Lac Caribou" are too common
  to place.

  WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT DO. It converts a vague lead into a located one. It does NOT settle
  the attribution: a seven-week camp six years established at Saint-Sauveur could have sent a
  party seventy kilometres north, and equally the High School of Montreal could have run its own
  trip there. THE TEST FOR THE NEXT PASS IS NOW SPECIFIC: does any Kanawana record -- the 1920s
  brochures, the Gas Bag runs, the directors' reports -- name Saint-Donat, Lac-Legendre, Lac
  Batiment, Lac McLaren or the Rouge-Matawin country? None of the nine lake names appears
  anywhere in this project's source cache outside this file.

  AND THE TEST WAS RUN, the same hour, and came back NEGATIVE. The cache was searched for
  Saint-Donat, St. Donat, St-Donat, Legendre, Matawin and Rouge-Matawin. NO KANAWANA SOURCE
  NAMES ANY OF THEM. The hits are all other things: "St. Donat" appears in Canadian Camping as
  OTHER camps' addresses in the 1975 directory and as a 1968 camp "situated at St. Donat in the
  Laurentians"; "Legendre" appears once in the 1988 YMCA annual report as a person, Esther
  Legendre. So the route country is absent from Kanawana's own literature as completely as the
  lake names are.

  CONCLUSION, recorded so the lead does not sit open tempting a later pass: "A Week in the Woods"
  IS NOT ATTRIBUTABLE TO KANAWANA on anything this project holds. Its country is seventy-two
  kilometres north of the camp and appears nowhere in the camp's records. What would reopen it is
  a Kanawana document this project does not yet have -- a 1910s trip log, a brochure of the
  period, or an early Gas Bag -- naming that country. Absent that, it is a High School of
  Montreal canoe trip printed in a High School of Montreal magazine, and the Kanawana
  advertisement on the following page is an advertisement.
